set.q: Rank the following 3 nuclei by increasing atomic radius: 1) Li^(+); 2) Na^(+); 3) K^(+)
Calculate the determinant of the 3x3 matrix with first row 2, 3, 4, second row 4, 3, 6, and third row 2, 6, 1.

A reaction has rate law of rate =k[A]^3[B]^-1[C]^4. Assuming the initial rate is R, If the concentration of A is tripled, the concentration of B is quartered, and the concentration of C is doubled, what is the new rate of the reaction in terms of R?

An industrial reactor carries out the exothermic Haber equilibrium 3 H_2 + N_2 ⇌ 2 NH_3. Identify all of the following three changes that increase the equilibrium amount of ammonia in a constant-volume vessel: 1) Decreasing temperature; 2) Adding helium; 3) Adding nitrogen
Which of the following choices best relates the function of DNA Polymerase I to DNA Polymerase III?
Given that x+1/x=6, find x^4+1/(x^4).
If p is prime, what is the value of Euler's totient function φ(p)?

In dihybrid crosses, a gene interaction known as recessive epistasis occurs where a homozygous recessive genotype at a certain locus masks the phenotypic expression of a different locus. This causes the typically phenotypic ratio to be different compared to that predicted by Mendel's Law of Independent Assortment. Which of the following is the phenotypic ratio expressed by recessive epistasis?
Rank the following 4 enzymes used in glycolysis in chronological order. 1) Enolase; 2) Phosphoglycerate kinase; 3) Hexokinase; 4) Phosphofructokinase
For how many positive values of x is 20/(x+1) + 20/(3(x+1)) a positive integer?
A 3 kg disk of radius 1.5 meters is rolling without slipping at a speed of 3 m/s. What are the sums of the velocities of the points at the top and bottom of the disk to the nearest tenth of a m/s?

Skyler is studying the reaction A+B → C with rate R. When he plots the natural log of concentration of A over time he gets a linear line and when he plots the inverse of concentration of B over time he gets a straight line. Knowing this he multiplies the concentration of A by 2.5 and quarters the concentration of B. What is the resulting rate of the reaction in terms of R?

Akhil submerses a cube of the new material in an ice bath until it reaches 273 K, then drops it in a bath of boiling water. If the material's coefficient of linear expansion is 2 × 10^-4 K^-1 and its volume in the ice bath is 2 m^3, what is its volume when it reaches thermal equilibrium with the boiling water to the nearest hundredth of a cubic meter?
In the hydrogen atom, a transition from n=3 → n=1 releases approximately how many times more energy than transition from n=2 → n=1?
Given that angle A = 20° and angle B = 25°, find the value of (1+tan A)(1+tan B).
Which of the following 3 reactions have an equilibrium constant K greater than 1 at STP? 1) 2NH_3(g) ⇌ N_2(g)+3H_2(g); 2) Cl(g) + e^(-) → Cl^(-); 3) Na^(+)(aq) + Cl^(-)(aq) ⇌ NaCl(s)
Rank the following three values in order of decreasing value. 1) sin(π/6) + tan(π/3); 2) e^3/2 + e^2/2 + e/2; 3) (2!/1! + 3!/2!)/8
For any positive integer n, denote f_1(n) as the square of the sum of the digits of n. For n ≥ 2, let f_a(n) = f_1(f_(a-1)(n)). Find f_1000(11).
What is the unit digit of the following number: 2008^(2007^2008) + 2007^(2008^2007)?
Let a be chosen uniformly from {1,2,...,200} and b be chosen independently and uniformly from {1,2,...,50}. What is the probability that b is greater than a?

A solenoid is constructed from 100 turns of copper wire. If the radius of the solenoid is 1 cm and its length is 100 cm, taking the permeability of free space to be 4π × 10^-7 H/m, what is the inductance of the solenoid in terms of π and in scientific notation?
A copper wire has a temperature coefficient of resistance of 3.93 × 10^-3 K^-1. If its initial resistance is 100 Ω at 250 K, what is its resistance at 450 K to the nearest tenth of an ohm?
Let N = (1!)^2(2!)^2(3!)^2⋯(100!)^2. What is the remainder when N is divided by 101?
Under analytic continuation of the Riemann zeta function, what is the value of ζ(-1)?
What is the sum of the last two digits of the expression: 1^3 + 2^3 + … + 2010^3?

An ionized nebula exhibits strong forbidden [O III] emission at relatively low electron density. As the electron density increases beyond the critical density of the transition, the forbidden line becomes weaker relative to an appropriate permitted recombination line. Which of the following best explains this behavior?

The differential form of Fourier's law of thermal conduction shows that the local heat flux density q is equal to the product of thermal conductivity and the negative local temperature gradient -∇ T. Given that the units of κ are W/(m · K), what are the SI units for the temperature gradient?

Using the integrated form of Newton's law of cooling, what is the surface temperature of a body with an initial temperature of 400 K, surrounding temperature of 280 K, and a positive cooling constant of (ln 2)/3 after 3 seconds to the nearest K?

Identify all of the following four types of stereochemical assignment that could correctly designate the absolute conformation of an atropisomer: 1) R_a and S_a; 2) E_a and Z_a; 3) P and M; 4) Δ and Λ
What is the integral from 0 to π/4 of the quantity sin(x) times tan(x) times sec(x)?
What is the sum of the absolute value of the spins of all the particle types in the standard model? Consider the W^(+) and W^(-) bosons as one boson and the 8 types of gluons as one boson.
Observation of the hypothetical process abbreviated 0νββ would provide strong evidence that neutrinos are their own antiparticles. What is this process called?
What is the indefinite integral of e^x cosh(x)?
What is arctan(1/2) + arctan(1/3)?

Identify all of the following three statements that are true about the harmonic sum ∑_(i=1)^n 1/i: 1) The series grows logarithmically as n increases without bound.; 2) If the sign of every other term is inverted, the series converges conditionally to (ln 2)/2.; 3) For all n > 2, the decimal value of the series never terminates.
Wolfgang loves 12-tet music. Let x be equal to the twelfth root of two. What is the closest integer to log_x(15/8)?
Let f^((n))(x) be defined as applying f to x a total of n times. What is the limit as n approaches infinity of sin^((n))(1)?

Using v=1/(√(μ_0μ_rε_0ε_r)) for a homogeneous, isotropic, nondispersive material, identify which of the following five constants appear in this expression for the phase velocity of light: 1) Fine Structure Constant; 2) Permeability of Free Space; 3) Permittivity of Free Space; 4) Planck’s Constant; 5) Relative Permeability of the Material

Seen in the image is a photomicrograph of seminiferous tubules and surrounding tissue. Answer the following three questions. 1) Identify the cell type labeled A. 2) Identify the cell type labeled B. 3) What type of cell junction between neighboring A cells forms the blood-testis barrier?
set.a.t: 1) SERTOLI CELL; 2) LEYDIG CELL; 3) TIGHT JUNCTIONS

set.q: Answer the following three questions about the image. 1) The image shows periodically spaced bands of a mineral precipitate formed as dissolved reactants diffuse through a medium. What named reaction-diffusion phenomenon produces this pattern of periodically spaced precipitation bands? 2) In the classical supersaturation model, which of the following best explains the formation of distinct bands rather than continuous precipitation: W) Precipitation occurs exclusively at the original interface between the two reactants; X) Local supersaturation triggers nucleation, depleting nearby reactants and delaying precipitation in adjacent regions; Y) Periodic fluctuations in the radioactive decay of the precipitate create gaps; Z) Diffusion coefficients alternate between positive and negative values? 3) After the bands have formed, smaller crystallites within the precipitate gradually dissolve while larger crystallites grow, even without additional reactants entering the system. Which of the following phenomena best explains this evolution: W) Spinodal decomposition; X) Kirkendall effect; Y) Ostwald ripening; Z) Constitutional supercooling?
Each quadrant in the Penrose diagram shown is labeled I, II, III, or IV. Name what region of spacetime each quadrant represents.
set.a.t: I) RIGHT EXTERIOR REGION; II) BLACK-HOLE INTERIOR; III) OTHER EXTERIOR REGION; IV) WHITE-HOLE INTERIOR

set.q: Answer the following three questions about the image. An exoplanet survey detects periodic decreases in brightness in a photometric aperture containing a bright target star and a faint neighboring star. 1) What class of astrophysical system can produce a false-positive exoplanet transit when its light is blended with that of a brighter neighboring star? 2) Difference imaging shows that most of the light lost during the apparent transit originates from the faint neighboring star rather than the target. Which conclusion is most strongly supported: W) The bright target definitely hosts a transiting planet; X) The dimming event most likely originates from the neighboring source rather than the bright target; Y) The neighboring source must be a white dwarf; Z) The transit depth must be independent of wavelength? 3) Suppose the neighboring eclipsing binary contributes 5% of the total light in the aperture, and its own flux decreases by 40% during an eclipse. What fractional decrease in the total measured flux is expected: W) 0.2%; X) 1%; Y) 2%; Z) 20%?

The image shows a diagram of an iterated function system fractal. The left side depicts the fractal itself in black, and the right side shows how the fractal is created: the entire fractal contained in the large gray square is equivalent to a scaled-up version of the regions of the fractal contained in each blue square. Answer the following two questions about this fractal. 1) What is the Hausdorff dimension of this fractal? 2) If the lower-left blue square instead filled the whole lower-left quadrant of the gray square, what would be the common name of the resulting fractal?

Answer the following two questions about the image. The compound in the image is undergoing a Beckmann rearrangement. 1) What specific functional group is made through the completion of this Beckmann rearrangement? 2) To which numbered carbon in the image is the nitrogen of this functional group attached?

Eight nodes are connected to one another as shown in the image. An ant begins at node 0, and every second moves clockwise about the center of the diagram to an adjacent node, choosing uniformly among the connected nodes. Answer the following two questions about the ant. 1) How many different paths can the ant take to return to node 0 for the first time? 2) What is the expected value of the node the ant is at after 4 seconds have passed?

The image depicts the Argand plane. A complex function f(z) has roots at the filled points and poles at the empty points. Answer the following three questions about f(z), given that each point in the graph has integer coordinates. Assume the plotted points are the only zeros and poles relevant to this question. 1) If f(z) is a rational function, what is the minimum possible sum of the degrees of the numerator and denominator? 2) What is the radius of convergence of the Maclaurin series for 1/f(z)? 3) Suppose that the residue at each pole of f(z) and 1/f(z) is equal to 2. Find the value of the contour integral of [f(z) − 1/f(z)] dz over the indicated contour C, traversed counterclockwise.
In physics, theory can only get you so far. What is the name of the experimental measurement device pictured?
Let N = (1!)^2(2!)^2(3!)^2⋯(100!)^2. What is the remainder when N is divided by 101?
